entries.subject: DAMIT 142: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-142.txt. Model 142, version 2011-04-20, pole (44°, 83°), period 8.28307 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: A. Marciniak (2008), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. V. 73 Klytia, 377 Campania, and 378 Holmia
entries.finding: [A. Marciniak (2008), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. V. 73 Klytia, 377 Campania, and 378 Holmia](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2008A%26A...478..559M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — excluded from physical scaling because the shape-aware VS-TPM fit is available. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 45.51 ± 0.52 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 73 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: New evidence invalidates the selected shape-aware thermal fit or establishes that an effective-sphere diameter is the appropriate physical scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model surveys: body-specific candidate not established
entries.finding: The imported survey cites Hanuš 2017, Viikinkoski 2017 and Vernazza 2021 without identifying a selected product for this body. The current DAMIT reference join does not bind selected model 142 to those surveys. This does not prove that no resolved model exists elsewhere; a body-specific candidate and its release must be identified before the entry can count as included.
entries.revisitWhen: A target row, supplementary model or release URL from one of these surveys establishes a concrete candidate and permits comparison with the selected shape.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — VS-TPM selected for this pole family; occultation ellipsoids are not silently substituted for mesh volume.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Only a uniform scale from the published thermophysical fit is transferred to the archived nominal mesh. The varied-model ensemble does not establish identical mesh bytes or local surface accuracy. The alternative pole remains possible. No thermal or reflectance map is inferred. Alternative archive solutions: model 143, pole ['266', '68'], [Model 143](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/143) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 143: pole (266°, 68°), 8.28307 h, version 2011-04-20. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
